title: Information in cognizable cases (FIR)
simple_explanation: Police must register information about a cognizable offence irrespective of where it occurred (Zero FIR). Information may also be given electronically (e-FIR), to be signed within three days. Informant gets a free copy.

title: When police may arrest without warrant
simple_explanation: Lists situations where police may arrest without a warrant; for offences punishable up to 7 years, arrest requires recorded reasons and a notice of appearance is generally issued instead.

title: Grounds of arrest and right to bail
simple_explanation: Person arrested without warrant must be told the full grounds of arrest, and, for bailable offences, of the right to be released on bail.

title: Informing relative or friend
simple_explanation: Police must inform a relative, friend or nominated person about the arrest and place of detention.

title: Right to meet an advocate
simple_explanation: Arrested person is entitled to meet an advocate of choice during interrogation, though not throughout.

title: Not to be detained beyond 24 hours
simple_explanation: Police cannot detain an arrested person beyond 24 hours (excluding journey time) without a magistrate's order.

title: Bail in non-bailable offences
simple_explanation: Court may grant bail in non-bailable offences; special consideration for women, children, sick or infirm persons.

title: Anticipatory bail
simple_explanation: Person apprehending arrest for a non-bailable offence can apply to the High Court or Sessions Court for a direction to release on bail if arrested.

title: Maximum detention of undertrial
simple_explanation: An undertrial who has served half the maximum sentence (one-third for first-time offenders, subject to conditions) is generally to be released on bail; not for offences punishable with death or life imprisonment.

title: Complaint to Magistrate when police refuse FIR
simple_explanation: If police refuse to register your FIR, you may send the complaint in writing to the Superintendent of Police (S. 173(4)) and then approach the Judicial Magistrate, who can order investigation.

title: Examination of witnesses by police
simple_explanation: Statements to police during investigation; women victims of certain sexual offences may have statements recorded at their residence by a woman officer.

title: Remand
simple_explanation: If investigation cannot be completed in 24 hours, the accused must be produced before a Magistrate; police custody is limited (generally up to 15 days in total, in parts).

title: Maintenance of wives, children and parents
simple_explanation: Magistrate may order a person with sufficient means to pay monthly maintenance to a wife unable to maintain herself, children, or aged parents (earlier CrPC 125).

title: Inherent powers of High Court
simple_explanation: High Court may quash FIRs/proceedings to prevent abuse of process or to secure the ends of justice (earlier CrPC 482).

title: Cheating
simple_explanation: Defines cheating and prescribes punishment, including for dishonestly inducing delivery of property.

title: Theft
simple_explanation: Defines theft and its punishment.

title: Cruelty by husband or relatives
simple_explanation: Cruelty to a married woman by her husband or his relatives is punishable (earlier IPC 498A).

title: Dowry death
simple_explanation: Death of a woman within seven years of marriage in abnormal circumstances, preceded by dowry-related cruelty.

title: Sexual harassment
simple_explanation: Defines sexual harassment, including unwelcome physical contact, demand for sexual favours and showing pornography against a woman's will.

title: Stalking
simple_explanation: Following or repeatedly contacting a woman despite disinterest, or monitoring her online activity, is stalking.

title: Criminal intimidation
simple_explanation: Threatening injury to person, reputation or property to cause alarm.

title: Defamation
simple_explanation: Making or publishing imputations intending to harm a person's reputation.

title: Rape
simple_explanation: Defines rape and prescribes punishment; consent obtained by fear or misconception is not consent.

title: Outraging modesty of a woman
simple_explanation: Assault or criminal force to a woman intending to outrage her modesty.

title: Insulting the modesty of a woman
simple_explanation: Uttering words, making sounds or gestures, or exhibiting objects intended to insult a woman's modesty.

title: Murder
simple_explanation: Punishment for murder: death or imprisonment for life, and fine.

title: Hurt and grievous hurt
simple_explanation: Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt, including by dangerous weapons or means.

title: Kidnapping
simple_explanation: Kidnapping from India or from lawful guardianship; aggravated forms cover minors and ransom.

title: Extortion
simple_explanation: Putting a person in fear of injury to dishonestly obtain property or valuable security.

title: Criminal breach of trust
simple_explanation: Dishonestly misappropriating property entrusted to you — covers many deposit/loan disputes with a criminal element.

title: Criminal trespass and house-trespass
simple_explanation: Entering another's property with intent to commit an offence or to intimidate, insult or annoy.

title: Forgery
simple_explanation: Making a false document or electronic record with intent to cause damage or support a false claim.

title: Intentional insult to provoke breach of peace
simple_explanation: Intentional insult giving provocation intended or likely to cause a breach of the peace.

title: Confession to police
simple_explanation: A confession made to a police officer cannot be proved against the accused.

title: Electronic records
simple_explanation: Conditions and certificate requirement for admissibility of electronic records as evidence.

title: Identity theft
simple_explanation: Fraudulent use of another person's electronic signature, password or unique identification feature.

title: Cheating by personation using computer
simple_explanation: Cheating by impersonation using a communication device or computer resource.

title: Violation of privacy
simple_explanation: Capturing, publishing or transmitting images of a person's private area without consent.

title: Obscene material online
simple_explanation: Publishing or transmitting obscene material in electronic form.

title: Compensation for data negligence
simple_explanation: A body corporate negligent in protecting personal data it handles is liable to pay compensation for wrongful loss or gain.

title: Hacking / computer-related offences
simple_explanation: Dishonest or fraudulent acts causing wrongful loss or damage using a computer resource — the general 'hacking' offence.

title: Cyber terrorism
simple_explanation: Acts threatening India's unity, integrity, security or sovereignty through computer resources; punishable with life imprisonment.

title: Sexually explicit content; child sexual abuse material
simple_explanation: Publishing/transmitting sexually explicit material (67A) or material depicting children in sexual acts (67B) online carries enhanced punishment.

title: Consumer rights
simple_explanation: Rights to safety, information, choice, to be heard, to seek redressal, and to consumer awareness.

title: Complaint before District Commission
simple_explanation: Manner of filing a complaint before the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission; can be filed electronically (e-Daakhil).

title: Limitation period
simple_explanation: A complaint must generally be filed within two years from the date the cause of action arose.

title: Request for information
simple_explanation: Any citizen may request information from a Public Information Officer in writing or electronically, without giving reasons.

title: Time limit for reply
simple_explanation: Information to be provided within 30 days; within 48 hours if it concerns life or liberty of a person.

title: Appeals
simple_explanation: First appeal to the senior officer, then second appeal to the Central/State Information Commission.

law_name: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
title: Complaint of sexual harassment
simple_explanation: An aggrieved woman may complain in writing to the Internal Committee (or Local Committee), generally within three months of the incident.

title: Maternity benefit
simple_explanation: Eligible women employees are entitled to paid maternity leave (up to 26 weeks for the first two children).

title: Payment of gratuity
simple_explanation: Gratuity payable on leaving employment after at least five years of continuous service (exceptions apply).

law_name: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
title: Application to Magistrate
simple_explanation: An aggrieved woman, Protection Officer or anyone on her behalf may apply to a Magistrate for reliefs such as protection, residence and monetary orders.

law_name: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
title: Reporting of offences
simple_explanation: Anyone who knows about a sexual offence against a child must report it to the Special Juvenile Police Unit or local police.

title: Drunk driving
simple_explanation: Driving with blood alcohol exceeding 30 mg per 100 ml (or under drugs) is punishable.

title: Duty to produce licence
simple_explanation: Driver must produce licence and documents on demand by an authorised officer; documents in DigiLocker/mParivahan are accepted.

title: Helmet compulsory
simple_explanation: Every person driving or riding on a two-wheeler must wear protective headgear (helmet).

title: Dangerous driving
simple_explanation: Driving dangerously, using a mobile phone while driving, or red-light jumping is punishable with fine and/or imprisonment.

title: Compensation for accident victims
simple_explanation: Victim or family of a road accident can claim compensation before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (MACT).

title: Divorce
simple_explanation: Grounds for divorce include cruelty, desertion (2 years), adultery, conversion, mental disorder; mutual-consent divorce under S. 13B after one year of separation.

title: Civil / inter-faith marriage
simple_explanation: Any two persons can marry under this Act regardless of religion, after a 30-day notice to the Marriage Officer.

title: Giving or demanding dowry
simple_explanation: Giving, taking or demanding dowry is punishable; the law applies to both sides.

law_name: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
title: Protection, residence and monetary orders
simple_explanation: Magistrate can pass protection orders, residence orders (right to stay in the shared household), and monetary reliefs including maintenance and compensation.

title: Atrocities against SC/ST persons
simple_explanation: Lists offences against members of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, including insults in public view, land grabbing and social/economic boycott; anticipatory bail is generally barred.

title: Payment of minimum wages
simple_explanation: Employer must pay at least the minimum wage fixed by the government for scheduled employment; paying less is an offence.

title: Timely payment of wages
simple_explanation: Wages must be paid before the 7th (or 10th, for larger establishments) of the following month; deductions are restricted.

title: PF contribution
simple_explanation: Employer and employee each contribute (generally 12% of wages) to the provident fund for establishments with 20+ employees; check balance via UMANG/EPFO portal.

title: Retrenchment conditions
simple_explanation: A workman with one year of service cannot be retrenched without one month's notice or pay in lieu, retrenchment compensation, and notice to the government.

title: Notice to quit (tenancy)
simple_explanation: A month-to-month lease can generally be terminated by 15 days' notice; a yearly lease by 6 months' notice, unless the agreement says otherwise.
